ruleName: Ball hits an outside influence or the player
title: Playing after your ball hits another person or animal
question: Your golf ball accidentally hits a person or an animal while in play. What does the rule say you should do?

choices.text: Add a penalty and replay the shot
Play the ball as it lies, no penalty
Drop a new ball near where the incident happened
Add two penalty strokes and continue

explanation: If your ball hits a person or animal by chance, you play the ball from where it rests with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What to Do If Your Ball Hits Someone or an Animal
juniorVersion.question: You hit your golf ball and it accidentally bumps into a person or an animal. What should you do next?

choices.text: Add a penalty and hit the shot again
Play your ball from where it stopped, no penalty
Drop a new ball nearby and play from there
Add two extra shots and keep going

juniorVersion.explanation: If your golf ball accidentally hits a person or animal, just play your ball from where it stopped. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Extra shots added to your score because of a rule mistake.

vocabulary.term: Play the ball as it lies
vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Hit the ball from where it finished after your shot.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Help kids learn that sometimes things happen by accident in golf, and the rules tell us what to do. Use soft toys or cones for safe practice when showing examples.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they always get a penalty if the ball hits something.
Some might try to hit the shot again instead of playing from where the ball stopped.
